cohort: 3006 first-time mothers in Pennsylvania between 2009 and 2011
finding: Racial/ethnic differences exist in cesarean delivery rates, and these differences are not explained by birth attitudes; white and high-socioeconomic status women may have a greater ability to realize their childbirth preferences.
mod_finding: Positive attitudes toward vaginal delivery were associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery, but this association was only significant for white, highly educated, and privately insured women.
